claims.reason: Evidence explicitly states a DeepSpace app is a normal Cloudflare Worker and apps deploy to Cloudflare Workers.
Evidence states DeepSpace deploys apps to Cloudflare Workers for Platforms via 'npx deepspace deploy', not Vercel. Vercel AI SDK is only referenced as a dependency for model typing, not deployment.
The evidence explicitly states that `npx deepspace deploy` builds and uploads the app, returning a live `<name>.app.space` URL.
Evidence states DeepSpace's integration proxy fronts 215+ third-party API endpoints, matching the claim.
Evidence explicitly states 'You don't store API keys, configure webhooks, or build per-vendor SDKs' when calling third-party APIs through DeepSpace's integration proxy.
The evidence section is empty, so there is no information to support or contradict the claim about developer-billed integrations and anonymous callers.
Evidence states the platform handles billing, rate-limiting, and provider routing for integration calls via integration.post, matching the claim that rate-limiting is handled by the platform.
Evidence states Google Workspace (google/*) endpoints require per-user OAuth and are always billed as 'user', with billing: 'user' set in src/integrations.ts, non-negotiable.
Evidence states permissions are enforced server-side in the Durable Object, checked before data ships over the wire, filtering records before WebSocket broadcast to clients.
Evidence explicitly states there is no 'anonymous' role; unauthenticated callers use the '*' wildcard key instead.
Evidence explicitly states 'New authenticated users get member by default' and the roles table lists member as default for all authenticated users.
Evidence shows useJobs returns jobs, enqueue, cancel, and retry functions, allowing clients to watch (jobs list), cancel, and retry background jobs.
No evidence was provided to support or contradict the claim about background job retry defaults.
Evidence confirms default alarm wall-time limit is 15 minutes, and listing a job type in backgroundJobTypes allows the handler to continue beyond that limit.
Evidence explicitly says to use Background Jobs instead of ctx.waitUntil for long AI generations, since waitUntil is killed 30 seconds after the response.
Evidence states DeepSpace can provision one managed Cloudflare AI Search instance per app, and an app may declare only one ai_search binding, matching the claim.
No evidence was provided to support or contradict this claim about knowledge search query character limits.
No evidence was provided to verify the claimed pricing of $0.825 per 1,000 queries for hybrid knowledge search.
No evidence was provided to verify any claims about scheduled tasks, cron expressions, or timezone handling.
Evidence states members and admins can fire owner-billed tasks by default, not only admins.
The reference doc states that when authToken is omitted, 'Owner pays - falls back to env.APP_OWNER_JWT', matching the claim.
Evidence states the default is 64,000 output tokens for Anthropic models, not 4,096.
No evidence was provided to support or contradict the claim about a uniqueOn constraint for enforcing one vote per user per poll.
Evidence describes DeepSpace's features (sync, presence, auth, etc.) and deployment on Cloudflare's global network, but makes no claim about scaling to millions of concurrent users out of the box.
The evidence provided is empty and contains no information about an SLA or uptime guarantee for DeepSpace.
The evidence describes DeepSpace's features and architecture but makes no mention of Firebase, pricing, or cost comparisons.
The evidence only states apps deploy to Cloudflare's global network so requests terminate close to the user; it does not mention any specific number of edge locations like 300+.
Evidence states DeepSpace ships a Stripe-backed payment system supporting subscription plans and one-time products, matching the claim.
